title: Fleet comparative flight data
usage: Historical evidence for comparison. Source type, applicability and test conditions are carried on each series. Comparison figures sharing a flight or source table belong to the same evidence.

sources.work: Technical Air Intelligence Center, Comparative Performance and Characteristics of Representative Enemy and Allied Aircraft, T304, third edition, June 1945
sources.primary_followup: Trace the aircraft columns through the source and definition notes on printed pp. 1–3. For US fighters retrieve the corresponding BuAer characteristics sheets or Army Materiel Command performance records. For German fighters retrieve the British A.I.2(g) summary and its underlying German trial.
sources.scope: Normal gross performance unless qualified. TAIC combined trials, guarantees and calculations and does not identify a test flight for each number. Both scans reproduce the same edition. Speed basis is unstated in the selected rows.

sources.work: Denis Richards, Royal Air Force 1939–1945, Vol. I, Appendix VI, British aircraft characteristics
sources.source_class: postwar British official history, secondary compilation
sources.primary_followup: Retrieve the underlying A&AEE and Air Ministry performance sheets for the wing, engine, rating, loading and test date.
sources.scope: Type summary. No individual aircraft, run loading or rating is stated.

sources.work: Denis Richards, Royal Air Force 1939–1945, Vol. I, Appendix VII, German aircraft characteristics
sources.source_class: postwar British official history, secondary compilation
sources.primary_followup: Trace Air Ministry performance sheets and identified CEMA, RAE or manufacturer trials for E, F, G and Fw 190 A configurations.
sources.scope: Type summary. No individual aircraft, run loading or rating is stated.

sources.work: USAAF, Performance Data on Fighter Aircraft, response to Major W. D. Hoyt, 25 July 1944
sources.primary_followup: The memorandum gives representative performance. Recover the originating maximum-power climb trials and fuel/weight/loading sheets for individual aircraft.
sources.scope: Page 2 paragraph d gives maximum-power climb at 10,000 ft. Table I elsewhere in the memorandum has different variants and conditions.

sources.work: Spitfire Vb W.3134, A&AEE brief performance trials
sources.source_class: period test report, secondary web transcription
sources.primary_followup: Locate the original signed A&AEE report and compare its tabulated figures, ditto marks and the pressure-head calibration to this transcription.

sources.work: Spitfire F IX BS.428, A&AEE level speed trials
sources.source_class: period test report, secondary web transcription
sources.primary_followup: Locate the original signed A&AEE report and compare its tabulated figures, ditto marks and the pressure-head calibration to this transcription.

sources.work: Spitfire LF IX MA.648, A&AEE SU injection pump level speed trials
sources.source_class: period test report, secondary web transcription
sources.primary_followup: Locate the original signed A&AEE report and compare its tabulated figures, ditto marks and the pressure-head calibration to this transcription.

sources.work: Spitfire HF IX EN.524, A&AEE propeller and reduction gear trials
sources.source_class: period test report, secondary web transcription
sources.primary_followup: Locate the original signed A&AEE report and compare its tabulated figures, ditto marks and the pressure-head calibration to this transcription.

sources.work: John M. Ellis III and Christopher A. Wheal, Ending the Argument, Sport Aviation, June 1990
sources.source_class: first-hand restored-aircraft trials, later web transcription and scanned figures
sources.primary_followup: Use the authors’ scanned figures for graph checks. For wartime application retrieve Republic, Goodyear/BuAer, Grumman and North American trials at matching power, mass and configuration.
sources.scope: Four restored aircraft on 100LL. Takeoff weight is reported. Mass at each test event is unspecified. The P-47 had its turbocharger removed. The report documents reduced allowable power.

sources.work: South Australian Aviation Museum History Group, Willy Messerschmitt – Messerschmitt Bf 109E, E-3 specification
sources.primary_followup: Retrieve the Messerschmitt E-3 / DB 601 Aa performance sheet behind these data. Compare loading and engine rating with the French CEMA trial of WNr 1304.
sources.scope: Printed p. 8. Aerodata gives overlapping speed and climb figures. Treat them as a shared lead. The E-3 specification gives two inconsistent units for the initial climb rate.

sources.work: Kennblatt für das Flugzeugmuster Bf 109, Baureihe F-1 und F-2 mit DB 601 N, Berlin 1941
sources.primary_followup: For a transfer to the simulator F-4, identify the corresponding DB 601 E F-4 performance sheet with climb rate and airspeed schedule. The F-1/F-2 share a DB 601 N here.

sources.work: Messerschmitt AG, Versuchs-Bericht 109 19 L 42, 19 September 1942, two engine and propeller installations in G-1 WNr 14026
sources.source_class: wartime manufacturer comparative flight report (original scan)
sources.primary_followup: The G-1 installation comparison is documented. For configuration-specific use follow the original G-2/G-6 engine and airframe reports and F-4 DB 601 E sheet.
sources.scope: Same G-1 airframe, each engine with its indicated VDM propeller. The installation changed with the engine. Blatt 1 reports speeds corrected to normal pressure and corrected regulator setting.

sources.work: US Navy, Project TED PTR-1107, comparative evaluation of Fw 190 A-4, F4U-1 and F6F-3, 1944
sources.primary_followup: Obtain longer stabilized speed runs or the individual test logs for each specimen when testing a maximum-speed claim. The printed report supplies its own loading, timing and power schedules.
sources.scope: Same test program, calibrated indicators. The two-minute runs were considered too short to establish maximum speeds. The prior research pack retained the turn test conditions from this report.

document_lineage.note: Only the common figures in the Bf 109 G and Fw 190 columns overlap. The original source chain is unresolved.
